title: Jessa's Name
summary: At Glasshouse, someone calls out a name from across the courtyard. For once the recognition is correct: Renna Iles knows Jessa from years before, immediately shifting the issue's center away from Kael.

panelPlan.text: Glasshouse is a low settlement of shaded courtyards and old translucent panels, social rather than futuristic in emphasis.
Renna Iles sees Jessa and shouts her name with genuine surprise. Jessa freezes more than Kael ever does at a false identity.
Eva looks at Kael out of habit, then realizes this has nothing to do with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: That is the part people usually mean by 'left.'

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: No, that is the part cowards mean by it.

directionInline.text: Correct recognition should feel more destabilizing to Jessa than false recognition ever feels to Kael. The issue belongs to her.

title: Before the Road
summary: Renna and Jessa fall quickly into old rhythms of affection and irritation. Eva learns that Jessa once spent enough time here to have routines, friends and unfinished conversations.

panelPlan.text: Renna drags Jessa through the courtyard pointing out what changed and what did not.
She remembers Jessa's old sleeping corner and a terrible meal they once made together. Jessa corrects every exaggerated detail.
Eva listens, amused by how much ordinary history exists behind the woman who presents herself as permanently in motion.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: You lived in that room for almost a year.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: You complained for almost a year.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You lived somewhere for four months?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I have survived many stationary periods.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: She cried when the cup broke.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I swore. There may have been moisture in my eyes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: This is the best town we've visited.

directionInline.text: Give Jessa ordinary history and humor. Her past should become real through mundane details rather than a withheld trauma dump.

title: You Leave Early
summary: Renna finally names the grievance beneath the reunion: Jessa tends to leave relationships while they are still good, before anyone can ask what comes next.

panelPlan.text: Renna and Jessa sit apart from the others after supper. Eva approaches, sees the tone and starts to leave; Renna invites her to stay.
Renna does not accuse Jessa of betrayal. She says the harder thing: Jessa leaves before anybody gets the chance to disappoint her or depend on her.
Jessa rejects the psychology, then admits she prefers departures she chooses.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: Stay. If she hates this enough, she can leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: I'm not saying you betrayed me, Jess. I'm saying everything was good, and you treated that like a deadline.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: It was starting to feel decided.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Everybody. Next season, next year, next room, next job. Like I had agreed because I hadn't objected yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: That was a very clear objection.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: To the rest of us it looked like an empty bed.

directionInline.text: Do not reduce Jessa to a diagnosis. Renna knows one pattern in her; she does not possess the final explanation.

title: Ask Jessa
summary: Eva asks Kael what he thinks happened between Jessa and Renna. Kael refuses to speculate and tells Eva to ask Jessa, modeling a different relationship to curiosity.

panelPlan.text: Eva finds Kael outside repairing a coat seam or cleaning dishes, away from Jessa and Renna.
She circles the question twice before asking what Jessa is not telling them.
Kael gives her no theory, only a boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: If I tell you what I think, you'll start listening to Jessa for proof of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: Then you have an answer to that question.

directionInline.text: Kael's ethical stance toward identity now teaches Eva outside the mystery. He can be perceptive without turning people into puzzles.

title: A Partial Answer
summary: Eva asks Jessa directly and receives a partial but honest answer: there was no secret catastrophe. Jessa left because staying was becoming a life she had not chosen.

panelPlan.text: Eva and Jessa walk through a quiet side courtyard while Renna gives them space.
Eva asks once, plainly, why Jessa left. She does not offer theories first.
Jessa says Glasshouse was good to her, which was part of the problem: everyone assumed good would become permanent.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I liked it here. That's the part nobody understands.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Why would that make you leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Because everybody started talking about next year like I had already said yes to it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Renna thinks that's the same thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: Renna is allowed to be wrong about me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Are you going to leave us like that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: I don't think so. That's the best answer I have.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You said it was the answer you had.

directionInline.text: The key growth is Eva accepting 'I don't know' without forcing a theory. Jessa's ordinary reason for movement becomes clearer but remains human and non-mythic.

title: One More Night
summary: Jessa chooses to stay one extra night for Renna's family supper even though the road is open and no crisis requires it. The choice matters because remaining is voluntary too.

panelPlan.text: The rig is packed before sunset. Renna invites Jessa to one family supper and makes no argument beyond wanting her there.
Jessa looks at the road, then unfastens one bag and carries it back inside.
Kael asks Jessa whether she wants to stay instead of deciding for her; Eva lets the answer stand without turning it into a theory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessa
dialogueInline.text: We can make the next stop before dark.

dialogueInline.speaker: Renna Iles
dialogueInline.text: You always leave when people try guilt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't trying to help. I asked.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kael
dialogueInline.text: That seems to be going around.

directionInline.text: Jessa's development is choice, not settling down. Staying briefly because she wants to is as important as leaving because she wants to.
